name: Mixing Water
description: There are two infinite sources of water: hot water of temperature $$$h$$$; cold water of temperature $$$c$$$ ($$$c \lt h$$$). You perform the following procedure of alternating moves: take one cup of the hot water and pour it into an infinitely deep barrel; take one cup of the cold water and pour it into an infinitely deep barrel; take one cup of the hot water $$$\dots$$$ and so on $$$\dots$$$ Note that you always start with the cup of hot water . The barrel is initially empty. You have to pour at least one cup into the barrel. The water temperature in the barrel is an average of the temperatures of the poured cups. You want to achieve a temperature as close as possible to $$$t$$$. So if the temperature in the barrel is $$$t_b$$$, then the absolute difference of $$$t_b$$$ and $$$t$$$ ($$$|t_b - t|$$$) should be as small as possible. How many cups should you pour into the barrel, so that the temperature in it is as close as possible to $$$t$$$? If there are multiple answers with the minimum absolute difference, then print the smallest of them.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$T$$$ ($$$1 \le T \le 3 \cdot 10^4$$$) — the number of testcases. Each of the next $$$T$$$ lines contains three integers $$$h$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le c \lt h \le 10^6$$$; $$$c \le t \le h$$$) — the temperature of the hot water, the temperature of the cold water and the desired temperature in the barrel.
output_specification: For each testcase print a single positive integer — the minimum number of cups required to be poured into the barrel to achieve the closest temperature to $$$t$$$.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1359C — Mixing Water [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
